title: Uber & Commercial Fleet Arbitrage

economics.includes_contractors_note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.
economics.revenue_basis: Gross weekly driver lease, commercial dispatch and co-hosting billings (55% retained contribution after investor owner splits & pass-through fleet costs)
economics.cost_basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.

regulatory_notes: Maintain continuous commercial livery / Period 1-2-3 rideshare coverage and airport TCP/TLC permits.
Observe state rental-car contract disclosures, toll pass-through rules and immobilizer safety laws.

plays.name: Uber Fleet Partner Portal Top-of-Waterfall Vehicle Lease & Livery Split Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Onboard eligible fleet vehicles and vetted drivers through Uber Fleet Partner Portal and configure authorized $425–$650 weekly lease charges and documented toll deductions ahead of driver payout where the local platform and law permit. The collection waterfall reduces manual billing but does not guarantee sufficient driver earnings, platform availability or permission for every deduction.
inputs: Locally eligible fleet vehicles with commercial registration, inspection records and continuous applicable livery or rideshare insurance
Vetted drivers with valid licenses, required permits, MVR screening and signed lease and deduction authorizations
Approved Fleet Partner account with verified local payout-split capabilities and vehicle-level toll and maintenance records
workflow: 1. Confirm local Fleet Partner eligibility, vehicle class requirements, insurance coverage and the legality of the proposed lease and payout structure.
2. Vet and onboard drivers, execute clear lease and toll disclosures and configure only supported, expressly authorized payout deductions.
3. Dispatch vehicles and reconcile trip earnings, weekly lease charges, toll evidence and driver balances against actual settlement reports.
4. Pay driver balances promptly, audit disputed deductions and schedule maintenance or vehicle reassignment based on utilization and safety data.
metrics: Collected weekly lease revenue per active vehicle against the $425–$650 target
Authorized lease and toll collection rate relative to amounts actually due
Vehicle contribution after insurance, maintenance, depreciation and downtime

platform_risks.failure_mode: Platform payout controls change or driver earnings cannot cover authorized lease deductions
platform_risks.trigger: Fleet account restriction, unsupported local deduction feature or persistently low driver utilization
platform_risks.impact: Collection shortfalls, driver disputes and negative vehicle contribution
platform_risks.detection_metric: Weekly unpaid authorized charges and settlement reconciliation exceptions per active vehicle
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend unsupported deductions, reconcile driver balances and use lawful disclosed invoicing or voluntary vehicle reassignment

plays.name: Commercial TLC/TCP Livery Plate & Two-Shift Black SUV Airport Dispatch Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Operate commercially registered Black SUVs using the locally applicable TLC, TCP or other livery authority across two separately staffed 10-hour shifts. Combine eligible Uber Black demand with independently contracted corporate airport transfers to improve utilization without assuming guaranteed surge pricing or treating jurisdiction-specific permits as interchangeable.
inputs: Eligible commercially registered Black SUVs with local livery authority, airport permissions and commercial insurance
Two qualified drivers per scheduled vehicle with verified credentials, rest compliance and documented shift handoffs
Authorized Uber Black access and independently sourced corporate transfer contracts with flight-aware dispatch
workflow: 1. Verify local commercial operating authority, airport access, vehicle eligibility and coverage for both app-based and direct-booked trips.
2. Staff two separate 10-hour driver shifts subject to applicable duty and rest limits, leaving time for inspection, charging or fueling and cleaning.
3. Allocate eligible app demand and direct corporate airport bookings using flight status, deadhead distance and confirmed pickup commitments.
4. Reconcile fares, driver compensation and airport fees, inspect each shift handoff and adjust schedules to measured contribution and safety performance.
metrics: Paid passenger hours as a percentage of available vehicle hours
Contribution per vehicle-day after driver pay, insurance, fuel, platform fees and maintenance
On-time airport pickup rate and deadhead miles per completed transfer

platform_risks.failure_mode: Permit, insurance or driver-duty noncompliance interrupts commercial operations
platform_risks.trigger: Expired credentials, uninsured trip category, prohibited airport pickup or fatigue-related scheduling exception
platform_risks.impact: Fines, denied coverage, vehicle suspension and lost corporate bookings
platform_risks.detection_metric: Upcoming credential expirations, uncovered-trip exceptions and duty-limit violations
platform_risks.fallback: Remove the affected vehicle or driver from dispatch and fulfill bookings through independently verified licensed and insured backup operators

plays.name: Zero-Owned-Metal Investor Vehicle Co-Hosting & GPS Starter-Interrupt Consignment
plays.mechanism: Manage investor-titled SUVs, hybrids and cargo vans for a contractually defined 25%–35% gross management split without owning the vehicles. Use professionally installed GPS/OBD-II telematics and, where lawful, a hardwired starter-interrupt with explicit notice and safe stationary-only controls. Maintain coverage matched to actual commercial use, including rideshare Periods 1, 2 and 3 where applicable and separate rental or off-platform coverage when needed.
inputs: Investor-titled vehicles with owner and lienholder permissions plus signed consignment agreements defining the gross management split
Use-specific commercial insurance verified for drivers, rentals, off-platform trips and applicable rideshare Periods 1, 2 and 3
Professionally installed GPS/OBD-II telematics and lawful starter-interrupt equipment with privacy consent and stationary-only safety controls
workflow: 1. Inspect each investor vehicle, verify title and financing permissions and execute a management agreement allocating maintenance, claims and revenue responsibilities.
2. Bind use-specific coverage and install disclosed telematics with access controls; prohibit remote engine shutdown or any immobilization while moving.
3. Place vehicles only with authorized vetted drivers or eligible booking channels and monitor utilization, maintenance needs and permitted location data.
4. Reconcile gross receipts, pay investor balances and the agreed management split, and coordinate lawful recovery or servicing only under documented safe procedures.
metrics: Earned management fees as a percentage of contractually defined gross vehicle receipts
Net management contribution per active investor-owned vehicle
Covered utilization days, unscheduled downtime and safety-control exceptions

platform_risks.failure_mode: Coverage gaps or unsafe telematics use create uninsured liability
platform_risks.trigger: Undeclared commercial use, an excluded driver or a starter-interrupt command without verified safe stationary conditions
platform_risks.impact: Injury exposure, denied claims, investor losses and termination of management contracts
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unverified coverage periods, unauthorized device access and rejected unsafe immobilization attempts
platform_risks.fallback: Disable remote immobilization, pause affected placements and arrange insurer-approved service or lawful professional recovery after safety review

plays.name: FMCSA/DOT New-Authority & Roadside Violation Trigger Funnels
plays.mechanism: Ingest daily federal FMCSA Census, Licensing & Insurance (L&I), and SMS roadside-inspection violation feeds to intercept newly granted MC/DOT authorities (during the mandatory 21-day insurance-filing window) and fleets with fresh HOS/maintenance citations.
inputs: FMCSA daily Licensing & Insurance (L&I) pending-authority feed
FMCSA Safety Measurement System (SMS) roadside violation & BASIC score logs
Commercial trucking insurance, factoring, & ELD compliance partner network
workflow: Poll daily FMCSA pending-application feeds to identify carriers that received a docket number but still need BOC-3 and BIPD insurance filings to go active
Monitor SMS inspection logs for fleets cited for ELD, hours-of-service, or maintenance violations requiring corrective action plans
Route carriers in real time to commercial truck insurance brokers ($500–$1,500 CPA/split), freight factoring desks, and compliance consultants
metrics: FMCSA filing-to-contact latency (minutes)
Pending-authority to bound-policy conversion %
Combined CPA from insurance, BOC-3, ELD, and factoring referrals

platform_risks.failure_mode: FMCSA government-impersonation enforcement or telemarketing DNC violations
platform_risks.trigger: Posing as the USDOT/FMCSA safety audit office or blasting automated SMS/robocalls to driver cell phones
platform_risks.impact: FTC/FMCSA enforcement warning and carrier spam blocking
platform_risks.detection_metric: Zero USDOT impersonation complaints and 100% carrier opt-in before SMS dispatch
platform_risks.fallback: Use transparent private compliance-agency branding, free BOC-3/MCS-150 status check tools, and inbound hand-raiser funnels

plays.name: Multi-Location Google Business Profile (GBP) Local-Pack Grid Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Capture high-margin Google Maps 3-Pack calls across tier-2/3 metros by partnering with real, licensed local tradespeople to co-verify legitimate physical office/shop locations, wiring call-tracking numbers and review-automation workflows to monetize excess lead capacity.
inputs: Geo-grid rank tracker identifying low-review-count Map Pack gaps in $3k+ home/commercial verticals
Joint-venture co-verification agreements with real brick-and-mortar licensed contractors
Dynamic call routing (Ringba) + automated SMS post-job review velocity loop
workflow: Identify suburban and tier-2 metro sub-markets where top-3 Google Maps competitors have <40 reviews and weak category optimization
Sign a revenue-share or pay-per-call partnership with a real local contractor or commercial office tenant (never using fake UPS boxes or virtual coworking addresses)
Optimize GBP primary/secondary categories, service-area pages, and automated customer review requests to lock top-3 Map Pack placement and bill per qualified call
metrics: Local Geo-Grid Top-3 share of voice (%)
Qualified inbound Map Pack calls per location per month
Net revenue per location ($1,500–$6,000/mo) and partner retention

platform_risks.failure_mode: Google Business Profile video-verification failure or network-wide account suspension
platform_risks.trigger: Creating fake storefront listings at UPS stores, virtual offices, or residential addresses without signage/licensing
platform_risks.impact: Immediate GBP suspension and loss of all accumulated reviews and Map Pack calls
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% physical signage, utility bill, and state contractor license verification readiness per profile
platform_risks.fallback: Only launch GBP profiles backed by a real partner's physical shop/yard capable of passing live video verification, and pair every listing with organic city rank-and-rent pages

plays.name: Rank-and-Rent Digital Real Estate & Pay-Per-Call Routing
plays.mechanism: Build and rank local high-ticket service hubs (foundation repair, water restoration, probate liquidation, commercial roofing) wired to dynamic call-tracking switches (Ringba / Twilio) that auto-bill local operators $75–$300 per inbound call lasting over 90 seconds.
inputs: City + high-ticket emergency/specialty service domain portfolio
Ringba / Twilio dynamic number insertion (DNI) & IVR duration billing switch
Co-verified local contractor partner agreements with card-on-file auto-recharge
workflow: Launch fast programmatic local service pages and cost calculators for high-ticket, high-urgency verticals ($5,000+ average job ticket)
Partner with a licensed brick-and-mortar operator in each city for legitimate Google Business Profile co-verification while retaining ownership of the domain and tracking numbers
Route inbound prospect calls through Ringba with a 90-second duration threshold, automatically charging the partner's card on file per qualified call
metrics: Inbound calls per site per month & % of calls >90 seconds
Revenue per qualified call ($75–$300) and contractor retention rate
Portfolio gross margin (80–90% once ranked)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Google Business Profile suspension or contractor payment default
platform_risks.trigger: Registering fake Google Maps pins at UPS stores/virtual offices or delivering calls before collecting prepaid credit balances
platform_risks.impact: Loss of Map Pack call volume or uncollected call receivables
platform_risks.detection_metric: Organic-vs-Maps call split and prepaid Stripe wallet balance per partner
platform_risks.fallback: Anchor traffic in organic city/calculator pages (immune to GBP suspension), co-verify Maps only with real partner physical addresses, and enforce prepaid auto-refill call wallets

plays.name: "Free LLC / Free Setup" Fintech Account Co-Registration Bounty Stacking
plays.mechanism: Offering a $0-service-fee LLC formation and business-launch concierge (borrower pays only mandatory state filing fees) that embeds a sequential post-formation 'Required Business Infrastructure Checklist' where every newly formed entity opens free business banking, corporate card, payroll, bookkeeping, and merchant accounts—yielding $600–$1,800+ in stacked B2B fintech CPA bounties per free formation.
inputs: High-intent 'free LLC formation' and 'start a business in [State]' search, social, and creator traffic
Automated state SOS filing workflow, EIN retrieval assistant, and operating-agreement generator
Direct B2B partner/CPA agreements with neobank, corporate card, payroll, and registered-agent providers
workflow: Acquire first-time founders via a genuine $0-markup LLC formation funnel where the user pays only state statutory fees
Guide the founder through an automated EIN and corporate-resolution wizard immediately upon state filing submission

Present an integrated 1-click onboarding sequence for a free business checking account ($150–$400 CPA), corporate charge card ($200–$500 CPA), payroll/bookkeeping trial ($100–$300 CPA), and web/domain host ($100–$200 CPA)
Provide automated compliance reminders and annual report tracking to capture recurring Year-2 registered-agent renewals
metrics: Stacked fintech CPA bounty revenue ($) realized per 100 free LLC formations
Post-EIN bank-account funding conversion rate (%) within 14 days of formation
Net customer acquisition margin after paid search/creator traffic spend

platform_risks.failure_mode: Fintech partner CPA clawback or payout tier downgrade due to unfunded/dormant business bank accounts
platform_risks.trigger: Sending low-intent formations that open free business bank accounts but never complete KYC or initial deposit funding
platform_risks.impact: Reversal of unvested CPA bounties or shift from account-open CPA to funded-account CPA tiers
platform_risks.detection_metric: 30-day funded-account activation rate (%) and average initial deposit balance across referred LLCs
platform_risks.fallback: Gate free operating-agreement and bookkeeping templates behind verified bank-account funding and pre-qualify founders on 30-day operating revenue intent

plays.name: Whitelisted Agency Ad-Spend Card-Multiplier Points & Volume-Rebate Cycling
plays.mechanism: Route genuine client-authorized advertising spend through eligible agency payment arrangements to earn contract-permitted rewards and volume rebates, net of financing, processing, and client pass-through obligations.
inputs: Client media mandates and rebate ownership clauses
Issuer reward categories, caps, and repayment terms
Platform invoices and agency volume-rebate agreements
workflow: 1. Verify client authorization, platform payment permissions, and ownership of rewards and rebates
2. Model eligible media purchases against reward caps, fees, liquidity, and rebate thresholds
3. Pay only genuine approved advertising invoices without circular spend or fabricated transactions
4. Reconcile settled rewards, client credits, refunds, and full card repayment each statement cycle
metrics: Net retained rewards and rebates per media dollar
Unfunded client exposure and repayment coverage
Invoice-to-reward reconciliation variance

platform_risks.failure_mode: Reward clawback or client-funded liquidity shortfall
platform_risks.trigger: Ineligible categories, prohibited payment aggregation, or delayed client reimbursement
platform_risks.impact: Lost rebates, interest costs, and card suspension
platform_risks.detection_metric: Denied reward value and overdue client balances versus cash reserves
platform_risks.fallback: Move to client-direct billing or prefunded approved agency terms and stop rewards-dependent spending

plays.name: High-Tier "Local Guide / Autoconfirmed Editor / Top Hunter" Authority Account Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Cultivating free user accounts into high-privilege algorithmic trust tiers—such as Google Local Guides (Level 6–10), Wikipedia Autoconfirmed/Extended-Confirmed editors, Product Hunt top hunters, and G2/Capterra/Trustpilot verified reviewers—whose edits, map suggest-an-edit actions, category changes, and launches carry massive algorithmic weight and sell for high-ticket B2B retainers.
inputs: Geo-matched Google Local Guide (Level 6+), aged Wikipedia, and aged Product Hunt / software-review accounts
Location-consistent EXIF metadata, mobile device telemetry, and verifiable third-party citation dossiers
B2B local-SEO, knowledge-graph, and SaaS launch client demand
workflow: Build sustained, legitimate contribution histories across local maps, encyclopedia entries, and software ecosystems to unlock elevated platform trust tiers
Use high-tier Local Guide accounts to submit rapid-approval GBP spam-name redressals, competitor duplicate merges, and category corrections for local-service clients
Execute policy-compliant, source-backed knowledge-graph updates and high-visibility Product Hunt/directory launches for B2B SaaS brands
Package these high-trust authority interventions as premium reputation, entity-SEO, and launch-management retainers ($2,500–$10,000/mo)
metrics: Platform edit/suggestion auto-approval rate (%) and time-to-live publication
Client local-pack rank lift or knowledge-panel entity resolution rate (%)
Retainer revenue per managed authority campaign ($)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Privilege-tier badge revocation or undisclosed paid-editing enforcement
platform_risks.trigger: Submitting biased, unsourced promotional edits or executing bulk map edits outside the account's natural geographic radius
platform_risks.impact: Demotion of account trust score and rollback of historical edits
platform_risks.detection_metric: Edit acceptance/revert ratio (%) and strict geographic/topical consistency per account
platform_risks.fallback: Submit only factually verifiable, secondary-source-backed edits and keep Local Guide accounts strictly locked to their native metropolitan areas

plays.name: Public-Record & API Intelligence
plays.mechanism: Ingest fragmented county dockets, probate registries, unclaimed property ledgers, and public APIs to surface uncontested claims or high-intent B2B triggers before manual competitors.
inputs: Court & probate dockets
State controller ledgers
Public licensing & entity APIs
workflow: Poll and normalize county/state record releases on an automated cadence
Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold
Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution
metrics: Cost per verified lead
Docket-to-contact latency (hours)
Net recovery / conversion rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating
platform_risks.trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals
platform_risks.impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry
platform_risks.detection_metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta
platform_risks.fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues
